definitions.gloss: practical work, actual business, hands-on work
definitions.explanation: The day-to-day practical tasks and operations of a job or organization, as opposed to planning, management, or theory.

examples.japanese: {実務|じつむ}{経験|けいけん}が{求|もと}められる。
{実務|じつむ}を{担当|たんとう}するのは{若手|わかて}の{社員|しゃいん}だ。
examples.english: The junior employees are in charge of the practical work.

examples.japanese: {理論|りろん}だけでなく{実務|じつむ}に{強|つよ}い{人材|じんざい}を{育|そだ}てたい。
examples.english: We want to develop people who are strong not just in theory but also in practical work.

notes:
{実務|じつむ} combines {実|じつ} (actual, real) and {務|む} (duty, work).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {実務|じつむ}{経験|けいけん} (practical work experience)
- {実務|じつむ}{者|しゃ} (practitioner, person in charge of operations)
- {実務|じつむ}{能力|のうりょく} (practical ability)
- {実務|じつむ}レベル (operational level)
- {実務|じつむ}{担当|たんとう} (person handling the actual work)

USAGE:
Commonly used in business and professional contexts. Often contrasted with {理論|りろん} (theory) or {管理|かんり} (management) to emphasize hands-on, operational work.
